newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan telecom privatisation consultant quits.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan telecom privatisation consultant quits.

text.p: A senior consultant at Pakistan's Privatisation Commission said on Tuesday he had resigned because of a "lack of clarity" on the long-delayed sale of the national telecom utility.
Zubair Ejaz, senior consultant on the privatisation of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL), confirmed a rumour that he had resigned on Monday.
Asked why, he said: "There is a lack of clarity on proceedings with the privatisation process (of PTCL)," he said. "When the situation is clear, I'll be happy to come back."

A spokesman for the Privatisation Commission declined to comment on Ejaz's departure, but said Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government was committed to its goal of selling a 26 percent stake in PTCL and transferring management control to a strategic investor by June 1998.

A commission source said the government had made no progress on the PTCL privatisation and had developed plans to invest 20 billion rupees ($492 million) in 1997/98 (July-June) to install new telephone lines despite opposition from financial advisers.

The source cited PTCL's annual report as saying the utility already had an installed capacity of more than 3.2 million lines at the end of 1995/96, but only 2.38 million working connections, a capacity utilisation rate of 74 percent.
He said it was unclear why the government wanted to add another half a million lines to installed capacity this fiscal year, when demand was projected at no more than 300,000 lines.
"The government in its own mind does not know what it wants to do with PTCL," added the source, who asked not to be named.
The original deadline for the sale of PTCL, regarded as the keystone of Pakistan's privatisation effort, was December 1995.
